title: Pretraining Augmentation Improves Fact Retrieval in Language Models
abstract: We pretrain language models with retrieval augmentation on an expanded corpus and find that fact retrieval accuracy improves substantially on held-out questions. Our evaluation uses the NaturalQuestions dataset and reports exact match accuracy. The gains hold across model sizes, but the improvement is smaller on out-of-domain questions.

title: Retrieval Augmentation Shows No Gain on Specialized Domain QA
abstract: We find that retrieval augmentation does not improve question answering accuracy on the BioASQ benchmark when the retrieval corpus lacks domain coverage. We evaluate exact match accuracy across three model sizes. Our results suggest that retrieval gains depend on corpus coverage rather than model scale.

title: Prompting Strategies for Multi-Hop Reasoning
abstract: We study prompting strategies for multi-hop reasoning on the HotpotQA benchmark. We find that decomposition prompts improve exact match accuracy by a large margin over direct prompting, and the improvement is consistent across five random seeds. Smaller models benefit more from decomposition than larger ones.

title: Scaling Laws for Downstream Task Fine-Tuning
abstract: We report that fine-tuning larger pretrained models yields diminishing returns on question answering benchmarks under a fixed compute budget. Our evaluation on SQuAD and NaturalQuestions shows accuracy gains that shrink as model size grows past two billion parameters. These results may suggest a compute-allocation trade-off for practitioners.

title: Evaluation Hygiene in Question Answering Benchmarks
abstract: We show that answer normalization and retrieval corpus leakage inflate reported exact match accuracy on standard question answering benchmarks. Across three widely used datasets, corrected evaluation reduces measured accuracy by up to nine points. We release an audit checklist for benchmark reporting.

title: Compact Distilled Models for On-Device Question Answering
abstract: We distill a retrieval-augmented teacher into a compact student model for on-device question answering. On the SQuAD dataset the distilled model retains most of the teacher accuracy while running within memory limits on a mobile device. Power consumption measurements suggest practical deployment is feasible.

title: Retrieval Corpus Quality Determines QA Gains
abstract: In controlled experiments we find that retrieval corpus quality determines downstream question answering gains more than retriever model choice. Using NaturalQuestions, we vary corpus coverage while holding the retriever fixed and observe monotonic accuracy changes. These findings are consistent with reports that coverage, not scale, drives retrieval benefits.

title: Uncertainty in Exact Match Reporting: A Replication Study
abstract: We replicate four question answering studies and find that reported exact match differences under one point fall within seed-to-seed variation. Confidence intervals across five seeds overlap in three of four comparisons. Our results suggest that small reported gains should be interpreted with caution.

title: Multilingual Retrieval Augmentation for Low-Resource Languages
abstract: We extend retrieval augmentation to low-resource languages where parallel corpora are scarce. Our evaluation on translated question answering sets shows that cross-lingual retrieval recovers part of the monolingual accuracy gap, though absolute accuracy remains lower than English results. Language coverage of the retrieval corpus remains the main limitation.

title: Negative Result: Chain-of-Thought Does Not Help Factual Recall
abstract: We find no measurable improvement from chain-of-thought prompting on factual recall questions, contrary to gains reported for mathematical reasoning. Across two question answering datasets the differences fall within noise. We release all prompts and evaluation scripts for scrutiny.
